summary: The operative verdict is the breaker's physical-selector cheat against the serialized multi-channel product factors. The builder's restricted pair-shell pass is genuine: two F_289 channels have rank three over F_17 on the frozen zero-margin transportation seam, detect the old weight-8 witness with syndrome (1,0,16,16), and leave no zero-syndrome malformed state among 7152 same-margin pair selectors below 17E. But every appended channel row is supported only on pair selectors. Holding the pair table fixed and flipping one physical NAND selector leaves all vector-transfer components zero. Exact search over r=1,2,3,4, both orientations, all legal cells, and 640 Hamming-one candidates finds such an attack in every one of 64 fibers at squared distance 20<306=17E, with E=18. This finitely kills the four unscaled 18-variable channel-prefix serializations, not unspecified extra/scaled rows or an absent maximal-order tile. Lean proves the universal conditional multi-channel algebra: nonzero componentwise division-ring transport preserves zero/nonzero syndrome, injective syndrome detects defects, r channels have exact F_17 dimension 2r, and above that capacity every linear syndrome has a nonzero kernel. Q1 and Q2 remain open; no hardness or dimension-gap claim follows.
hypothesis: Selected the sole cross-review overlap, Fable Proposal 2 / corrected Pro Proposal 1: a direct sum of rank-one F_289 product transfers. Causal mechanism: r channels provide 2r residue coordinates, so two channels can inject the frozen three-dimensional pair-seam defect space and componentwise division-ring transport cannot erase a nonzero vector syndrome. Expected frontier move: remove every zero-syndrome malformed vector below 17E in the fully serialized tile. Falsification condition: any unrestricted subthreshold malformed state with zero residual in every channel. The same-margin pair shell passes, but a physical-selector Hamming-one flip meets the falsification condition in every tested factor.

Across r=1 through 4, both orientations, and 64 legal fibers, exact search of 640 physical Hamming-one candidates finds in every fiber a zero-vector-transfer NAND-selector flip at squared distance 20<306=17E.
Both deterministic Python verifiers compile successfully.
Mathlib compiles the transport equivalence, injective-syndrome detection theorem, exact 2r channel finrank, injective rank bound, and above-capacity kernel theorem.

Its emitted transfer or sufficiently scaled Euclidean rows must cover physical NAND/COPY deviations as well as pair selectors while preserving saturated equal-energy legal fibers. Hash-lock all rows, centered lifts, factors, targets, both orientations, DROP and false targets, and common E. Run exact physical Hamming-one and Hamming-two searches first, then enumerate the complete unrestricted shell below 17E and recompute the enlarged zero-syndrome Graver basis.
